note: Class: not yet attackable; a rival to the reading of the premise more than a sourced counterexample. Unattributed: Newton's first law (STMT-NEWTON-LEX-I-CHANGE-OF-STATE-ONLY-BY-IMPRESSED-FORCE, sourced) is conditional and requires an impressed force only for a change of state; it asserts no force-free moving body. The rival adds that such a body exists and that its uniform motion is a being moved in the sense of DEF-MOTION-AS-REDUCTION. The Thomist reply is that a state of uniform motion is no reduction from potency to act. Missing: a disambiguation of local motion as state versus reduction under DISAMB-MOTION, and a source that asserts the existential.
